quest.title: Next Time, On King of Invokations...
quest.description: Something seems to be bothering the novelist, Fukumoto...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x25000

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: *sigh* I want to go back to Inazuma... How could this happen to me...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Traveler? *sigh* Don't even mention the novel. Those researchers working on Genius Invokation TCG are barely holding it together.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: According to a researcher I know quite well, the team encountered all kinds of problems that could only be described as baffling...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: For example, a Haravatat researcher suddenly asked a question one day.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: He said that if the effect descriptions on the cards are too long, it might discourage people who aren't used to reading long blocks of text from playing the game.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Researchers are used to reading large chunks of text and aren't affected by this issue, but the long descriptions could very well turn potential players away.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: So he suggested cutting the amount of text on some cards in half to make them easier to read.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: It's not a problem to me... But the researchers are still working hard on this issue. After all, it's about the player's experience, and the fewer problems, the better.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Anyway... There's an even bigger problem. They promised to help me find models for my novel, but something went wrong with that, too.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Remember? I told you earlier about a researcher who said they'd introduce me to Tighnari and Cyno, and ask them to be the inspirations for my novel.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: But they're so busy. I don't think I can count on them for a while...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: The researcher who received me was not able to help me with this, but he gave me an idea.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: He said Cyno sometimes goes to Puspa Café to play cards.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: If I want... I can try my luck there first. Or maybe they'll help me get in touch when they're free.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And... what are your thoughts?

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: *sigh* By the time they're free, I'll have finished writing the novel.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: I guess I'll go myself and see if I can find Cyno.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: But if I'm lucky enough to meet Cyno at the café, how should I even introduce myself to him? What a dilemma...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Really!? That's amazing! But how did you... Uh, you know what? I'm not gonna pry further.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: What are we waiting for then? Let's head to Puspa Café right now! Hope we'll be able to catch Cyno...

choices.text: How will you get in touch?

talks.objective: Meet up with Fukumoto at Puspa Café

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Shh... I—Isn't that Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Look at his outfit, his hairstyle, and that hair color... This is exactly what a protagonist in a card game novel should look like!

choices.text: This has no rhyme nor reason...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Heh, just trust my instincts on the market. But now's not a good time to explain...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Traveler, please ask Cyno to be the model for my novel... I'm counting on you!

choices.text: I actually know quite a lot of people who can fit into this category...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Really? That's great. I'm working on the third book of "King of Invokations," and this time, I'm not going to base it on the gameplay mechanics of Genius Invokation TCG.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: I'm going to create an all-new way of playing. For instance... I could get all cards to be suspended mid-air on the field. Players will have to collect cards as they consider their next move, all the while preventing their opponent from collecting cards themselves...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Hahaha! I'm getting excited just thinking about it! But we don't have time for this right now...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, this combination of cards isn't so bad.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But they're not strong enough to deal with quick attacks...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you up to, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? I didn't expect to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm in the middle of trying to build a Genius Invokation deck with a relatively slow attack speed.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm hoping that the deck would allow the player to obtain an abundance of resources and plenty of powerful cards...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But to be honest, it's hard to build a deck like that...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Currently, in the Genius Invokation TCG community, some players prefer to use cards with fast attack speeds.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: At the beginning of the game, they play a large number of cards in one go in order to swiftly defeat their opponent.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But I'm no fan of this tactic. I prefer to continuously accumulate resources in different ways...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Seizing every possible opportunity, building up my advantage, and eventually securing the victory...

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Yes, yes! Wonderful! You're just like the main character in my novel!

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Sorry! Uh... I'm...

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Hello, General Mahamatra. I don't suppose you've heard of me...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I've read your novel. It's very good.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: I'm truly honored!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: In the novel, every time the protagonist is at a disadvantage, he always manages to get a card that wasn't in his deck through various means, then defeats his opponent. This left a lasting impression on me.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I understand that writing novels requires taking a creative license, but this way of winning is a departure from the fundamental mechanics of Genius Invokation TCG.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: About that, well... Although I do play Genius Invokation TCG a lot, I'm not really good at it... And if you write about the duels with a competitive mindset, it wouldn't make for an interesting story.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Hmm, is that so? Well, as luck would have it, I've just built two decks of cards, so we can play a few rounds of Genius Invokation TCG here. Maybe you'll find some inspiration.

choices.text: (Now they are about to play cards...)

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: Eh? Playing with... with you? I'd love to, but the truth is...

choices.text: (This guy simply wants to play cards...)
This is the author of "King of Invokations."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You take several pictures of Cyno very quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: This has been a big help. I'm sure Asagiri will make an excellent illustration!

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Thank you very much, Cyno. I'll be sure to send you a copy of the novel as soon as it's published.

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Uh, Cyno, the two decks you're holding are...?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Didn't you promise to play a few games of Genius Invokation TCG with me earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Eh!? I—I'm not very good at it, so uh... Traveler! You're definitely better than me!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Then the matter is settled. Here, take this quick attack deck.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I'm going to use this relatively slower deck to see how I can deal with your attacks.

response.speaker: Fukumoto
response.text: I'll do my best, Cyno...

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Cyno, your play style is so... slow and deliberate...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: It's just an intuitive strategy.
